answer: Every quartz crystal ticks at its own slightly wrong rate, so the network can fingerprint hosts by clock skew. Each epoch, 40 VRF-timed signed pings ask a key for its raw monotonic tick count; a fit against network time gives skew in ppm. VMs share one host crystal, so keys within 0.2 ppm merge into one seat. Software can fake a skew, so the fit must also follow the parabolic temperature drift implied by public weather at the declared site; a flat basalt-cellar rack fails. Each alias needs its own board and site, about $40 a month, so 50 aliases cost $2,000: saffron prices per vote.
